BURHAN:v3p284/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p284/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p284/r4.claim: In the first passage من قومه precedes the adjective to clarify who the speakers are before the long description; the other passage follows the ordinary order.
BURHAN:v3p284/r4.anchor: فقدم المجرور على الوصف لأنه لو أخبر عنه وأنت تعلم أن تمام الوصف بتمام ما يدخل عليه الموصوف

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.claim: After recalling worldly blessings, the surah tells of Noah's struggle against his people's denial and rebuke and his journey in the ark.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.anchor: the sūrah narrates the story of Noah, his struggles with the denial and rebuke of his people, and his journey in the ark (vv. 23–41)

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r7.claim: The waw before وقال الملأ here links the leaders' false speech to the messenger's true statement, marking their contrast; its omission in al-Aʿrāf and Hūd makes the speech an independent answer to an implied question.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r7.anchor: وجاء هنا وقال الملأ بالواو. وفي الأعراف وسورة هود في قصه بغير واو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r8.claim: The phrase لقاء الآخرة means meeting the afterlife's reward and punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r8.anchor: بلقاء الآخرة أي بلقاء الجزاء من الثواب والعقاب فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r9.claim: أترفناهم means that God gave them ample hopes and provisions and made them comfortable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r9.anchor: وأترفناهم أي بسطنا لهم الآمال والأرزاق ونعمناهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r10.claim: أترفناهم may be joined to the description of those leaders, making their denial despite God's favor its cause; alternatively it is circumstantial, with the same implication that they denied the messenger while being treated well and should have been grateful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p558/r10.anchor: واحتملت هذه الجملة أن تكون معطوفة على صلة الذين،

TABATABAI:23:23-54/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r9.claim: The chiefs’ arguments arise from their denial of monotheism, prophecy, and resurrection together with their indulgent worldly life.
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r9.anchor: وقد نشأت هذه الأقاويل من اجتماع الصفات التي وصفهم الله به في أول الآيات وهي إنكار التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد والإتراف في الحياة الدنيا

TABATABAI:23:23-54/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r10.claim: The opening phrase places “of his people” before “who disbelieved,” unlike the previous story; this preserves the parallel order of “disbelieved,” “denied,” and “were indulged,” whereas placing it later would make the phrase too long.
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r10.anchor: لأنه لو وقع بعد { الذين كفروا } اختل به ترتيب الجمل المتوالية { كفروا } { وكذبوا } { وأترفناهم }

SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r1.claim: If mā is a relative pronoun, the object pronoun is omitted; the deletion meets the conditions because preposition and governor match, no nominative is displaced, and no other pronoun remains.
SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r1.anchor: هذا إذا جعلناها بمعنى الذي فإن جعلتها

SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r2.claim: If mā is a verbal noun, it needs no resumptive pronoun, and the verbal noun occupies the object position, meaning what they drink.
SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r2.anchor: فإن جعلتها مصدرا لم تحتج إلى عائد

SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r3.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ is reported as construing the phrase with an omitted min, as though it said they drink from it; al-Samīn says this extra preposition is unnecessary.
SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r3.anchor: وزعم الفراء أن معنى " ما تشربون " على حذف أي:

SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r4.claim: Al-Samīn rejects the claim that this deletion is barred for Basran grammarians: the conditions are met, though omitting min from the relative construction loses the partitive parallel with what they eat.
SAMIN-DURR:23:33/r4.anchor: يعني أنه يقدر: تشربونه من غير حرف جر

ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r1.claim: The people's elite reject truth and the afterlife amid worldly ease and plenty, which has corrupted them.
ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r1.anchor: the great ones among his peopl e, who refused to acknowledge the truth and gave the lie

ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r2.claim: They dismiss the messenger as an ordinary human and reject his promise that people will be raised after becoming dust and bones.
ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r2.anchor: nothing but a mortal like yourselves

ASAD-NOTES:23:33#n18/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:33#n18/r1.speaker: Tabari
ASAD-NOTES:23:33#n18/r1.claim: Tabari explains the phrase as saying that God granted them ease and plenty in worldly life; Asad points to his fuller discussion of tarifa at 11:116.
ASAD-NOTES:23:33#n18/r1.anchor: Thus Tabari interprets the concise but meaningful phrase atrafnahum fi 'l-hayati 'd-dunya.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r1.claim: He calls the passage's close with resurrection natural: resurrection is the final link in the sequence of life and its development.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r1.anchor: فأنتَ ترى أن ختام الآيات هذه بالبعث، هو الختمُ الطبيعي، وهو الحلقة النهائية في سلسلة الحياة وتطورها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r3.claim: Al-Muʾminūn repeatedly invokes death, resurrection, and the afterlife, as shown by its references to resurrection, return to God, denial of the hereafter, and life's alternation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r3.anchor: أما جو سورة المؤمنون فشائعٌ فيه ذِكْرُ الموت والبعث

ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r1.claim: Al-malāʾ refers to the community's leading nobles.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r1.anchor: وقال الملأ ( أي الأشراف ( من قومه ( بيان لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r2.claim: The phrase من قومه identifies which nobles are meant; the following clause describes them as unbelievers who deny the afterlife, its judgment and recompense, resurrection, or the second life.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى الذين كفروا وكذبوا بلقاء الآخرة أي بلقاء ما فيها من الحساب والثواب والعقاب

ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r3.claim: The unbelief clause may distinguish these nobles if other nobles in that generation believed; its wording also serves to disparage them.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r3.anchor: صفة للملأ جيء بها ذما لهم وتنبيها على غلوهم في الكفر ويجوز أن تكون للتمييز

ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r4.claim: One syntactic explanation says من قومه precedes the descriptive clause to avoid separating the identifying phrase from its noun or creating a misleading attachment.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r4.anchor: وتقديم ( من قومه ) هنا على الصفة مع تأخيره في القصة السابقة لئلا يطول الفصل بين البيان والمبين

ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r5.claim: An objection says there is no need to make الذين modify the nobles or explain the word order, since it can plainly modify قومه.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r5.anchor: مع ظهور جواز جعله صفة لقومه ورد بأن الداعي

ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r6.claim: A reply favors making God gave them luxury part of the relative clause: it then describes the nobles semantically, consistent with the customary depiction of chiefs as affluent; it may also be a circumstantial clause from كذبوا.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r6.anchor: على الصلة فيكون صفة معنى للموصوف بالموصول والمتعارف وإنما هو وصف الأشراف بالمترفين

ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r7.claim: أترفناهم means that God granted them ease and abundance in worldly life.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī does not accept that only chiefs are customarily described as affluent; even if that were usual, the clause can be a circumstance of the nobles, with or without قد.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r8.anchor: وأنت تعلم أنا لا نسلم أن المتعارف إنما هو وصف الأشراف بالمترفين ولئن سلمنا فوصفهم بذلك قد يبقى

ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r9.claim: Although conjunction to the relative clause is grammatically apparent, making God's enrichment a circumstance of the nobles' state is more eloquent because it intensifies blame for mistreating their benefactor.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r9.anchor: نعم الظاهر لفظا عطف جملة ( أترفناهم ) على جملة الصلة والأبلغ جعلها حالا من الضمير لإفادته الإساءة إلى من أحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r10.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r10.claim: Al-Kashf explains the waw here as marking contrast between the messenger's statement and the recipients' reply, reported as their talk among themselves; elsewhere a direct exchange permits a resumptive narrative.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r10.anchor: وجيء بالواو العاطفة في ( وقال الملأ ) هنا ولم يجأ بها بل جيء بالجملة مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r11.claim: Al-Ālūsī says this does not resolve why one passage narrates the contrast and the other the exchange; reversing the waw and asyndeton would also create variation, and he sees no clear reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r11.anchor: ولا يحسم مادة السؤال إذ يقال معه : لم حكى هنالك المقاولة وهنا التفاوت بين المقاتلين ولم يعكس

ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r12.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r12.claim: One proposed reason for waw here versus fa in Noah's story is that this group's speech did not immediately follow their messenger's speech, unlike Noah's people.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r12.anchor: وأما الإتيان بالواو هنا والفاء في ( فقال الملأ ) في قصة نوح عليه السلام فقد قيل : لعله

ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r13.claim: The nobles' question intensely belittles the messenger by reducing him to a human like themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p29/r13.anchor: ولا يخفى ما في قولهم ( ما هذا ) الخ من المبالغة في توهين أمر الرسول عليه السلام وتهوينه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r1.claim: The eating and drinking clauses establish the claimed likeness between the messenger and his people.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r1.anchor: تقرير للمماثلة والظاهر أن ( ما ) الثانية موصولة والعائد إليها ضمير وجرور حذف مع الجار

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r2.claim: The second ما is apparently relative, with its genitive resumptive and preposition omitted as permitted by the same conditions as مررت بالذي مررت; the clause-ending rhyme helps.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن ( ما ) الثانية موصولة والعائد إليها ضمير وجرور حذف مع الجار لدلالة ما قبله عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r3.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ is said to posit deletion of the genitive resumptive together with its preposition, which Basran grammarians disallow.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r3.anchor: وفي التحرير زعم الفراء حذف العائد المجرور مع الجار في هذه الآية وهذا لا يجوز عند البصريين

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r4.speaker: التحرير
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r4.claim: Al-Taḥrīr proposes either no deletion if ما is a verbal noun, or deletion only of an object pronoun if ما is relative, in keeping with Basran rules.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r4.anchor: والآية إما لا حذف فيها أو فيها حذف المفعول فقط لأن ما إذا كانت مصدرية لم تحتج إلى عائد

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the Basran alternatives lose the eloquence of parallel constructions; either analysis also needs interpretive effort because the speaker drinks another individual of the same kind, not the very same drink.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30/r5.anchor: وهذا تخريج على قاعدة البصريين ويفوت عليه فصاحة معادلة التركيب على أن الوجه الأول محوج إلى تأويل المصدر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r1.claim: They denied the eventual return to the afterlife.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r1.anchor: كذبوا بلقاء الآخرة} أي المصير إلى الآخرة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r2.claim: Atarna-hum means that God favored them with comforts and abundance.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r3.claim: The phrase means that the messenger eats and drinks what they eat and drink.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r3.anchor: يأكل مما تأكلون منه ويشرب مما تشربون

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r5.claim: The wāw may signal that their speech did not directly follow the messenger's speech, unlike the renewed speech of Noah's people; the explanation assumes a question.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r5.anchor: لعله ذكر بالواو لأن كلامهم لم يتصل بكلام الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r6.claim: They denied either the reward and punishment of the hereafter or resurrection into a second life.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r6.anchor: بلقاء ما فيها من الثواب والعقاب، أو بمعادهم إلى الحياة الثانية بالبعث

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r7.claim: They were made luxurious through abundant wealth and children.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r7.anchor: ونعمناهم { في الحياة الدنيا } بكثرة الأموال والأولاد

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r8.claim: The notables insist the messenger shares their human nature and condition; his eating and drinking as they do reinforces that likeness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r8.anchor: في الصفة والحالة. { يأكل مما تأكلون منه ويشرب مما تشربون

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r9.claim: The repeated mā is relative; its link in the second clause is omitted, either as an accusative pronoun or with its preposition understood from the first.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:31-33/r9.anchor: تقرير للمماثلة و «ما» خبرية والعائد إلى الثاني منصوب محذوف أو مجرور حذف مع الجار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r1.claim: This continues the pattern of Noah’s people failing to believe and fear God; the conjunction makes this account a stronger consolation for the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r1.anchor: فلم يؤمنوا ولم يتقوا داب قوم نوح

BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r2.claim: Al-malaʾ are the eminent chiefs whose appearance fills the onlookers’ chests.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r2.anchor: أي الإشراف الذين تملأ رؤيتهم الصدور

BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r3.claim: Putting “from his people” first emphasizes and specifies the consolation; it also avoids placing it after the long relative clause.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r4.claim: Their disbelief means they covered up what they knew from the proofs of divine oneness and the punishment of idolaters.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r4.anchor: غطوا ما يعرفون من أدلة التوحيد والانتقام من المشركين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r5.claim: Their denial of meeting the Hereafter is denial of resurrection.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r6.claim: Worldly luxury, often mistaken for happiness, usually blocks afterlife felicity by fostering insolence, ingratitude, and arrogance even toward the Benefactor.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r6.anchor: قاطع في الغالب عن سعادة الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r7.claim: They point to the Messenger with “this” to belittle him before their audience.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r7.anchor: أشاروا إليه تحقيرا له عند المخاطبين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r8.claim: They allege that he resembles them in creation and condition, implying no distinction that could make him a messenger.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r9.claim: They cite his eating ordinary food and drinking ordinary drink to argue that he cannot be a messenger above them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r9.anchor: من شرابها فكيف يكون رسولا دونكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r1.claim: The elite’s speech is coordinated with the preceding account instead of being introduced as a separate dialogue turn, unlike the usual reported-conversation pattern.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r1.anchor: عطفت حكاية قول قومه على حكاية قوله ولم يؤت بها مفصولة كما هو شأن حكاية المحاورات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r2.claim: They address their own people to stop the messenger’s appeal influencing the public, judging that this intervention matters more than replying to the messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r2.anchor: ما هنا كلامهم الموجه إلى خطاب قومهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r3.claim: Their reply is delayed: after the messenger continued repeating his call, they turned to their people, so the speech takes waw rather than the immediate-response fa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r3.anchor: لأن قولهم هذا كان متأخرا عن وقت مقالة رسولهم التي هي فاتحة دعوته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r4.claim: The messenger’s call is reported with explanatory أن after the sending, not with a direct قال quotation; this also helps explain the different connective form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p50#2/r4.anchor: كلام رسولهم لم يحك بصيغة القول بل حكي ب ( أن ) التفسيرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r1.claim: Elsewhere the people of Hud and Salih answer their messengers directly with rejection and rebuke, as shown in the cited replies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r1.anchor: حكى الله في آيات أخرى عن قوم هود وعن قوم صالح أنهم أجابوا دعوة رسولهم بالرد والزجر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r2.claim: الذين كفروا is a second adjective of الملأ, parallel to the wording about Noah’s elite; it is delayed so the following coordinated descriptions can attach to it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r2.anchor: نعت ثان ل { الملأ } فيكون على وزان قوله في قصة نوح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r3.claim: لقاء means one person’s presence with another; here it means meeting God for reckoning, and its attachment to الآخرة means meeting in the Hereafter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r3.anchor: واللقاء : حضور أحد عند آخر . والمراد لقاء الله تعالى للحساب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r4.claim: الإتراف is making people live in luxury, and ترف means abundant blessing; Ibn Ashur points back to its earlier treatment in al-Anbiyaʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r4.anchor: والإتراف : جعلهم أصحاب ترف . والترف : النعمة الواسعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r5.claim: Their denial of the Hereafter removes fear of postmortem accountability, while wealth breeds arrogance and attachment to ruling rather than following; these traits help explain their rejection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52/r5.anchor: وفي هذين الوصفين إيماء إلى أنهما الباعث على تكذيبهم رسولهم لأن تكذيبهم بلقاء الآخرة ينفي عنهم توقع المؤاخذة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52#2/r1.claim: Calling him merely a human like them is a metonym for denying his prophetic claim: they state the supposed premise that humanity excludes messengership and intend that conclusion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52#2/r1.anchor: كناية عن تكذيبه في دعوى الرسالة لتوهمهم أن البشرية تنافي أن يكون صاحبها رسولا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52#2/r2.claim: Eating and drinking what they do serve as evidence for his ordinary humanity; the object pronoun after تشربون is omitted because its equivalent appeared in the preceding relative clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52#2/r2.anchor: وجملة { يأكل مما تأكلون منه } في موقع التعليل

BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r1.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r1.claim: Al-Raghib defines the malā as a group united by an opinion, whose presence fills eyes with awe and souls with grandeur.
BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r1.anchor: قال الراغب : الملأ الجماعة يجتمعون على رأي فيملؤون العيون روعاء والنفوس دلالة وبهاء

BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r2.claim: The malā are the leading figures of the disbelieving people; their description as disbelievers censures them.
BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r2.anchor: أي أشراف قومه الكافرين وصفوا بالكفر ذما لهم

BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r3.claim: The conjunction wāw rather than fa is used because their speech does not follow directly from the messenger's speech; truth and falsehood coincided, far apart in value.
BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r3.anchor: وذكره بالواو دون الفاء كما في قصة نوح لأن كلامهم لم يتصل بكلام الرسول

BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r4.speaker: برهان القرآن
BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r4.claim: Unlike the Noah passage, this verse places min qawmihi first because its relative clause is longer; delaying the prepositional phrase would confuse the syntax and putting it mid-clause would be awkward.
BURSEVI:v6p58#2/r4.anchor: قال في "برهان القرآن" : قدم من قومه في هذه الآية وأخر فيما قبلها

BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r1.claim: They denied arrival in the afterlife through resurrection and gathering, or denied meeting its accounting, reward, and punishment.
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r1.anchor: بالمصير إلى الآخرة بالبعث والحشر أو بلقاء ما فيها

BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r2.claim: God made them comfortable and expanded their worldly ease; the root describes luxuriating in abundance, which can lead to arrogance.

BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r3.claim: The chiefs spoke to their descendants, misleading them, on account of their abundant wealth and children.
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r3.anchor: بكثرة الأموال والأولاد أي قالوا لأعقابهم مضلين لهم

BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r4.claim: This refers to Hud, whom the chiefs portray as sharing ordinary human qualities with them.
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r4.anchor: أي : هود {إلا بشر مثلكم} في الصفات والأقوال البشرية

BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r5.claim: His eating and drinking the same food as them is offered as proof that he is merely human; their Persian gloss argues a prophet should resemble angels and need neither food nor drink.
BURSEVI:v6p58#3/r5.anchor: أي تشربون منه وهو تقرير للمماثلة

BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r9.speaker: النبي ﷺ
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r9.claim: The Prophet says the believer eats in one intestine and the disbeliever in seven.
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r9.anchor: قال النبي عليه السلام : "المؤمن يأكل في معى واحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r3.claim: God made them prosperous, expanding their hopes and provisions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r3.anchor: وأترفناهم معناه نعمناهم وبسطنا لهم الآمال والأرزاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r4.claim: Their objection repeats the idea that a messenger cannot be human, as in Noah's people's rejection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r4.anchor: ومقالة هؤلاء أيضا تقتضي استبعاد بعثة البشر وهذه الطائفة وقوم نوح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r5.claim: The passage does not state that a miracle appeared and was then denied, but that sequence is understood even though the particular miracle is unspecified.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r5.anchor: لم يذكر في هذه الآيات أن المعجزة ظهرت لهم وأنهم كذبوا بعد وضوحها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r6.claim: Punishment applies only after someone abandons an obligation, and following a messenger becomes obligatory once proof is established for the person or intended audience.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r6.anchor: والعقاب لا يتعلق بأحد إلا بعد تركه الواجب عليه، ووجوب الاتباع إنما هو بعد قيام الحجة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r7.claim: Proof established through the Qurʾān for Arabs, Jesus' miracles for physicians, and Moses' signs for magicians establishes the case for those who follow them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p142#2/r7.anchor: الجمهور كالعرب في معجزة القرآن والأطباء لعيسى، والسحرة لموسى، فبقيام الحجة على هؤلاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#2/r2.claim: God sent one of their own people to call them to worship Him alone; the leaders rejected him because he was a human like them and they themselves ate and drank as he did.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#2/r2.anchor: وأنه تعالى أرسل فيهم رسولا منهم، فدعاهم إلى عبادة الله وحده لا شريك له. فكذبوه وخالفوه، وأبوا من اتباعه لكونه بشرا مثلهم،

JISHUMI:v7p5045/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5045/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5045/r9.claim: إتراف means indulging in pleasures; a مُترَف is left free to do as he wishes without restraint.
JISHUMI:v7p5045/r9.anchor: والإتراف: التنعم بضروب الملاذ، والترفه: النعمة، والمترف: المتروك يصنع ما يشاء

JISHUMI:v7p5046/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r2.claim: The wāw in وقال الملأ links successive statements, as though one speaker said one thing and then another.
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r2.anchor: فأرسلنا لم حذفت الفاء وأدخلت الواو في قوله: (وقال الملأ)

JISHUMI:v7p5046/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r13.claim: The ملأ are the community’s leading and prominent people.
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r13.anchor: وقال الملا من قومه يعني الأشراف الذين كفروا بالله

JISHUMI:v7p5046/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r14.claim: Meeting the Hereafter means resurrection and judgment, or meeting the promised recompense.
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r14.anchor: وكذبوا بلقاء الآخرة أي: بالبعث والجزاء، وقيل: بلقاء ما وعدهم من الجزاء

JISHUMI:v7p5046/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r15.claim: God gave these people worldly comforts and abundant ease.
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r15.anchor: وأترفناهم في الحياة الدنيا أي: نعمناهم فيها، ووسعنا عليهم نعيم الدنيا

JISHUMI:v7p5046/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r16.claim: The chiefs argue that the messenger is an ordinary human who eats and drinks as they do, and that following him would mean loss.
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r16.anchor: ما هذا الرسول إلا بشر مثلكم يأكل مما تأكلون منه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188/r1.claim: Without wāw, the accounts in al-Aʿrāf and Hūd answer an implied question; the wāw here connects their statement to the prior one, showing truth and falsehood together in stark contrast.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188/r1.anchor: على تقدير سؤال سائل قال : فما قال قومه ؟ فقيل له : قالوا كيت وكيت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188/r2.claim: Meeting the Hereafter means meeting what it contains of reckoning, reward, and punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188/r2.anchor: بلقاء ما فيها من الحساب والثواب والعقاب ، كقولك : يا حبذا جوار مكة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188/r3.claim: A pronoun is omitted; the sense is “from your drink,” or the pronoun is understood from what precedes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188/r3.anchor: حذف الضمير ، والمعنى : من مشروبكم ، أو حذف منه لدلالة ما قبله عليه

MUQATIL:23:31-34/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:31-34/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:31-34/r4.claim: The malaʾ are the chiefs or prominent members of the people.

MUQATIL:23:31-34/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:31-34/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:31-34/r5.claim: The chiefs rejected God's oneness and denied resurrection, where deeds would be repaid; they had been made prosperous in worldly life.
MUQATIL:23:31-34/r5.anchor: يعنى بالبعث الذى فيه جزاء الأعمال

MUQATIL:23:31-34/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:31-34/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:31-34/r6.claim: The chiefs mean Hud is merely a human like them and has no superiority; he eats and drinks as they do.
MUQATIL:23:31-34/r6.anchor: يعنون هودا، عليه السلام، { إلا بشر مثلكم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r1.claim: The elite speaking are from Hud’s people, and their speech answers his call.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r1.anchor: ﴿ وقال الملأ من قومه ﴾ ذكر مقالة قوم هود

NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r2.claim: In al-Aʿraf and Hud, “they said” lacks a conjunction because an imagined question prompts the answer; here wāw coordinates their words with the Messenger’s, presenting truth and falsehood together rather than a direct reply. Noah’s story uses fa because the elite’s speech immediately answers what preceded.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r2.anchor: فى الاعراف وهود بغير واو لأنه على تقدير سؤال سائل قال فما قومه فقيل له قالوا كيت وكيت وههنا مع الواو

NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r3.claim: “Who disbelieved” may describe the elite or the whole people.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r4.claim: They denied the encounter with everything in the Hereafter, including reckoning, reward, and punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r4.anchor: أى بلقاء ما فيها من الحساب والثواب والعقاب وغير ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r5.claim: God made them prosperous in worldly life with abundant wealth and children.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r5.anchor: ﴿ وأترفناهم ﴾ ونعمناهم ﴿ في الحياة الدنيا ﴾ بكثرة الاموال والأولاد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r6.claim: “This” refers to the Prophet; they argue that he cannot claim God’s message because he is a human like them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r6.anchor: ﴿ ما هذا ﴾ أى النبى ﴿ إلا بشر مثلكم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r7.claim: The second “from it” is omitted after “drinks from what you drink,” since the preceding wording makes it understood.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p121#7/r7.anchor: أى منه فحذف لدلالة ما قبله عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r1.claim: Al-malaʾ means the community's nobles, leaders, and chiefs.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r2.claim: Denying the meeting with the Hereafter means denying resurrection and judgment.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r3.claim: God's granting them worldly abundance made them insolent; atrafnāhum comes from tarfa, luxury like a fine gift.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r3.anchor: أي وسعنا عليهم نعم الدنيا حتى بطروا

QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r4.claim: The chiefs argue that the messenger has no advantage over them because he needs the same food and drink.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r4.anchor: فلا فضل له عليكم لأنه محتاج إلى الطعام والشراب كأنتم

QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r5.claim: Al-Farra says an omitted min is understood: “he drinks from what you drink from.”
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r5.anchor: على حذف من، أي مما تشربون منه

QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r6.speaker: البصريون
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r6.claim: Basran grammarians reject the need to omit min: if mā is a verbal noun it needs no resumptive pronoun; if relative, the object is simply omitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r6.anchor: ولا يحتاج إلى حذف ألبتة لأن «ما» إذا كان مصدرا لم يحتج إلى عائد

RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r3.claim: Rāzī identifies three traits of the people: disbelief in the Creator, denial of the Hereafter, and immersion in worldly luxury; he glosses their being made affluent as being favored.
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r3.anchor: هي شر الصفات : أولها : الكفر بالخالق

RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r4.claim: In this context, making them affluent means granting them worldly ease and favor.
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r4.anchor: وقال الملا من قومه } أي نعمناهم

RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r5.claim: The accounts without a conjunction answer an implied question about what the people said; the conjunction here coordinates their false speech with the prophet's true speech.
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r5.anchor: الذي بغير واو على تقدير سؤال سائل قال فما قال قومه

RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r6.claim: The conjunction in this account conveys that the true and false speeches occurred together in the same episode.
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r6.anchor: وأما الذي مع الواو فعطف لما قالوه على ما قاله

RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r7.claim: Their first objection is that the messenger is a human who eats and drinks as they do; they treat obedience to him as a loss because it brings no return benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r7.anchor: أي من مشروبكم أو حذف منه لدلالة ما قبله عليه

RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r8.claim: They call following a human messenger a loss despite not considering idol worship a loss.
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r8.anchor: ولئن أطعتم بشرا مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون

STUDYQURAN:23:33/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:33/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:33/r1.claim: The notables fear that Noah wants to rule over them.
STUDYQURAN:23:33/r1.anchor: the notables’ fear is that Noah desires to rule over them

STUDYQURAN:23:33/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:33/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:33/r2.claim: Being given luxury refers to receiving ease and privilege.
STUDYQURAN:23:33/r2.anchor: Whom We had given luxury in the life of this world refers to those who were granted ease and privilege

STUDYQURAN:23:33/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:33/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:33/r3.claim: The rejection of a messenger’s ordinary human life recalls disbelievers’ reported complaint about Muhammad eating and walking in markets.
STUDYQURAN:23:33/r3.anchor: See also 25:7, where the disbelievers reportedly say of the Prophet Muhammad, What ails this Messenger, who eats food and walks in the markets?

TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī identifies the prophet sent after Noah as Ṣāliḥ and his people as Thamūd.

TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r2.claim: The people who disbelieved were those who denied God's oneness.

TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r3.claim: Denying the meeting with the Hereafter means denying meeting God in the next life.
TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r3.anchor: يعني: كذبوا بلقاء الله في الآخرة

TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r4.claim: God gave them ease, broad livelihood and abundant provision in worldly life, until they became insolent, rebellious against their Lord, and disbelievers.
TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r4.anchor: يقول: ونعمناهم في حياتهم الدنيا بما وسعنا عليهم من المعاش وبسطنا لهم من الرزق، حتى بطروا وعتوا على ربهم وكفروا

TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites a rajaz poet's line «وقد أراني بالديار مترفا» as evidence that the word conveys being made affluent or luxurious.
TAB-FULL:v17p39#3/r5.anchor: ومنه قول الراجز: وقد أراني بالديار مترفا

TABRISI:23:35-40/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35-40/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:35-40/r7.claim: The chiefs denied resurrection and recompense.

TABRISI:23:35-40/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35-40/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:35-40/r8.claim: God had granted the chiefs worldly luxury and varieties of pleasure.

TABRISI:23:35-40/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35-40/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:35-40/r9.claim: They argue their messenger eats and drinks like them and so has no greater claim to prophethood.

THALABI:v7p46/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p46/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p46/r4.claim: God’s enriching the elites means granting them comforts and abundance in worldly life; tarf means blessing.
THALABI:v7p46/r4.anchor: وأترفناهم نعمناهم ووسعنا عليهم، والترفه: النعمة، في الحياة الدنيا

THALABI:v7p46/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p46/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p46/r5.claim: The elites reject the messenger as a mere human who eats and drinks as they do, and warn that obeying him would make them losers.
THALABI:v7p46/r5.anchor: قال الملأ من قومه الذين كفروا وكذبوا بلقاء الآخرة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p297#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p297#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p297#2/r1.claim: Atrafna means that God gave them abundance until they became luxurious; turfa is linked with tuḥfa, as a pampered person is one given gifts.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p297#2/r1.anchor: أترفناهم في الحياة الدنيا} وسعنا عليهم حتى أترفوا،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:27-33/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:27-33/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:27-33/r9.claim: God made the affluent leaders comfortable and gave them abundant means.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400/r6.claim: God's granting them ease in worldly life means that He expanded their provision.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400/r6.anchor: وسعنا الدنيا عليهم، أي في الرزق

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400/r7.claim: The chiefs argued that Hud was a human like them who ate and drank as they did, and that obeying him in his call would make them losers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400/r7.anchor: ما هذا إلا بشر مثلكم يأكل مما تأكلون منه ويشرب مما تشربون

ELMALILI:23:31-41/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r3.claim: Unlike the account of Noah's people, this one highlights denial of the Hereafter and arrogant indulgence in worldly luxury, traits Elmalılı also sees in contemporary unbelievers.
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r3.anchor: bunların hakkında ise küfürleriyle beraber âhiret likāsını tekzib ve hayât-ı dünyada nimet ile şımarıklık hasletleri de bilhassa zikredilmiştir.

ELMALILI:23:31-41/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r4.claim: The chiefs deny human prophethood by reducing the prophet to an ordinary person who eats and drinks as they do.
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r4.anchor: beşerî risaleti kabul etmemekle beraber peygamberi alelâde bir beşer seviyesinde göstermek için beşeriyeti yiyip içtiği şeylerle mukayese ediyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r5.claim: Opponents of prophets were often wealthy elites content with the order because it served their interests; they feared afterlife accountability and a society conscious of universal rights and justice would threaten their status.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r5.anchor: bunlar umumiyetle hak peygamberin getirdiği sistemi kendi toplumsal ve ekonomik statüleri için tehlikeli görmüşler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r6.claim: They tried to discredit prophets as ordinary humans lacking extraordinary divine credentials, distracting people from the religious and moral truth of their message.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r6.anchor: peygamberin görünürdeki insanî özelliklerini abartılı ifadelerle öne çıkararak insanların dikkatlerini peygamberin tebliğlerindeki dinî ve ahlâkî ilkelerde bulunan gerçekliğe

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.claim: Since the Qur’an answers these denials of the prophet’s person and of the afterlife elsewhere, this passage only warns of the rejecters’ painful fate.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.anchor: burada bir defa daha tekrarlanmasına gerek görülmemiş, sadece uğrayacakları acı âkıbete dikkat çekilmekle yetinilmiştir

BURHAN:v3p162/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p162/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p162/r4.claim: The author rejects treating “he drinks from what you drink” as object deletion, since the verb drink can take an object directly.
BURHAN:v3p162/r4.anchor: وهو فاسد لأن شرب يتعدى بنفسه

BURHAN:v3p233/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p233/r3.speaker: السكاكي
BURHAN:v3p233/r3.claim: Al-Sakkaki says من قومه is advanced before الذين كفروا to prevent the phrase seeming to describe worldly life; another verse safely delays it because the ambiguity is absent.
BURHAN:v3p233/r3.anchor: وجعل السكاكي 2 من الأسباب كون التأخير مانعا
